key_insight: TREX automates the entire LLM fine-tuning lifecycle by orchestrating two specialized agents (Researcher and Executor) using agent-driven, tree-based exploration to plan, search, and execute training workflows end-to-end.
problem_solved: Manual LLM fine-tuning is time-consuming, error-prone, and hard to scale across complex, open-ended research workflows (requirement analysis, literature/data search, experiment design, and iterative training). TREX targets end-to-end automation of these steps.
method: Multi-agent architecture: a Researcher agent generates objectives, plans, and exploration branches while an Executor agent runs experiments, pipelines, and evaluations.
Agent-driven tree-based exploration: systematic branching, pruning, and iterative feedback to explore design choices (data, formulas, hyperparameters, protocols) efficiently.
Automated orchestration of the full training lifecycle: from requirement analysis and open-domain research to data collection, experiment execution, and iterative fine-tuning.
impact: TREX can significantly cut human effort and turnaround time for LLM development, improve reproducibility of training workflows, and enable practitioners to scale and iterate on model fine-tuning with less manual coordination.

paper_title: TREX: Automating LLM Fine-tuning via Agent-Driven Tree-based Exploration
paper_authors: Zerun Ma, Guoqiang Wang, Xinchen Xie, Yicheng Chen, He Du
